Candl is a birthday reminder app to help individuals keep track of their contacts’ birthdays. When a user signs up for Candl, they must provide their phone number and birth day and month. They can also grant Candl access to contacts in their address book; if they do, Candl will store the phone number(s) and birth day and month, if any, associated with each of those contacts. When a user gives the app access to contact information in their address book, if that user has the Birthday Network feature enabled, Candl stores and periodically syncs from that address book each contact’s day and month (but not year) of birth in its Birthday Network in association with the contact’s phone number; the app does the same for the user’s own birth day and month. If another Candl user has the Birthday Network feature enabled and gives Candl access to the same contact without an associated birthday, Candl will share the prevailing birthday from the Birthday Network with that other Candl user.

Because Candl is designed to collect only limited personal data, Baron App has little insight into the contacts included in the Birthday Network or the app users accessing that data, and does not independently verify the identity of app users beyond validating that they can receive text messages at the phone number they use to sign up for the app. Users of the app must represent and warrant that they will not use Candl, and will not assist or encourage any third party to use Candl, to access or attempt to access any information (including birthdays and phone numbers) associated with any individual they do not personally know, and that they will not use Candl, and will not assist or encourage any third party to use Candl, to extract, export, withdraw, or otherwise remove any information from the Candl app or attempt to do any of the foregoing.

2. Maintaining and licensing access to a database of information concerning celebrities, the overwhelming majority of which is "publicly available" information under the CCPA.

Use #1 attracts large numbers of opts outs from selling/sharing, which are received through Famous Birthdays' consent management platform (including via global privacy control) and processed instantaneously. 

Use #2 attracts very modest numbers of requests to delete from the profiled celebrities, which are processed manually. Please note that it is only use #2 that qualifies Famous Birthdays as a data broker. 

Information is being provided about both uses because we understand that to be required, but we would note that conflating the two kinds of data uses is more likely to confuse consumers than it is to inform them.

Separately, we'd ask that the CPPA uses its regulatory authority to reduce the burdens this process places on small businesses like Famous Birthdays that only barely qualify as Data Brokers under the law and appear to be on the margins of what the State is seeking to regulate with this process. The reporting could be better directed to only those uses implicated by a business' data brokerage operations, and could also levy fees that are better tailored to business' ability to pay. On the latter score, note that the current fees are extremely onerous on small business.

Unacast places an emphasis on being open and transparent about our data processing activities. Our team is regularly available to address and discuss any privacy concerns regarding our services. A copy of our regularly-updated privacy policy is also available on our website.

We comply with all privacy requests received. If a record is in our system, we take the requested action (to delete, opt-out and/or to know). Additionally, we add all privacy requestors to a secure, hashed opt-out list regardless of whether they were already in our system to ensure we do not collect their data again in the future. Therefore, we report 100% compliance with all privacy requests.

Details regarding our data collection and usage are available in our  privacy policy: https://www.unearthcampaigns.com/privacy-policy/

We do not collect personal information directly from consumers. USADATA licenses/ resells audience datasets from major third-party compilers (e.g., Acxiom, Data Axle, Epsilon) and processes them under contract. We do not create or maintain an independent consumer database, and we do not enrich records beyond quality assurance. Where a provider or client indicates a consumer has opted out, we do not sell or make that consumer’s information available. Consumers should submit access/opt-out/delete requests directly to the original data providers or the originating business; we will honor those signals and propagate suppressions accordingly.
To learn more, visit veeva.com/privacy

Venntel places an emphasis on being open and transparent about our data processing activities. Our team is regularly available to address and discuss any privacy concerns regarding our services. A copy of our regularly-updated privacy policy is also available on our website.

Vi delivers integrated, specialized data science and analytics capabilities tailored to healthcare organizations, including providers (e.g., hospitals and health systems), pharmaceutical/biopharma companies, and wellness companies. Vi's platform focuses on delivering measurable ROI through enhanced patient activation, engagement, operational efficiency, and outcomes.
Vi collects and processes data from customer sources, publicly available sources, and select trusted third-party partners. We provide clients with tailored audience segments to support retention, outreach, acquisition, and performance objectives - these segments include mobile advertising identifiers and hashed email addresses.

We have a national data file license that we purchase national data on all real property in the US of which is public data - assessor data, mortgage and history data, tax data, real property data.   We also obtain phone and email data from a national data provider and we do not collect consumer data directly form consumers.   We purchase all our data from national data providers

VRTCAL Markets is a Service Provider to publishers (mobile apps, mobile websites, CTV) acting as an intermediary to deliver digital advertisments. VRTCAL does NOT interact directly with consumers so it contractually requires publishers to obtain proper consent and only send ad requests that have consent to our platform. VRTCAL does not store and only passes on mobile advertising IDs and CTV IDS of consumers to advertising partners providing the digital ads. Thus we have no data to delete.

Wurl provides content distribution and advertising services to streaming platforms and content companies. We receive and pass connected TV identifiers to advertisers. Wurl has no direct relationship with end user viewers.

Since 2024 we have expanded the request types to include limitation of sensitive data use.  We direct people seeking more information to our privacy policy.  Also note that during 2024 we received a large number of apparently bogus requests, resulting in a significant proportion of "denied" requests.  These were not formally denied, but they were not completed due to email verifications not being completed.  We are able to see that a large number of these requests pertained to non-existent email addresses.

ZS is a business consulting firm that mainly provides services to healthcare companies; we do not provide people finder services as an example. ZS operates as a data broker in very limited ways in relation to professional contact details and professional opinions of healthcare professionals.
